## Core idea

Maintain disjoint equivalence classes as edges or unions arrive.

The first question is which input features make this technique appropriate and which repeated work it can eliminate.

## Worked-problem starting point

Count connected components after adding undirected links.

Formulate input and output precisely, trace a miniature example, and state the invariant before writing an implementation. If the mathematical abstraction below is only a model, identify its assumptions.

## Mathematical Abstraction

$$
connected(u,v)\iff find(u)=find(v)
$$

This relation is an entry point to formal reasoning, not a universal complexity guarantee for all problems carrying the **Union-Find** label. Define the symbols, domains and any assumptions in the context of the problem being solved.

## Learning and verification workflow

1. Choose the smallest representative input and record the intended output.
2. Derive an operation or algorithm maintaining a clearly stated invariant.
3. Give a correctness argument, such as induction, an exchange argument, graph properties, or a state-machine invariant.
4. Analyse worst-case or expected time and memory, specifying the data structure and input assumptions.
5. Test boundaries, repeated values, invalid conditions, and a counterexample to a naive implementation.
